title: Critical Search
subtitle: Configure the rules to identify potentially sensitive files

fileRules.title: File Rules
fileRules.description: Define which files are considered critical
fileRules.keywordsHelp: Files that contain these words in their name will be considered critical
fileRules.extensionsHelp: Files with these extensions will always be considered critical
fileRules.exactNamesHelp: Files with these exact names will be considered critical
fileRules.mimeTypesHelp: Files with these MIME types will be considered critical
fileRules.excludedHelp: Files with these extensions will be IGNORED in the critical search (e.g. binaries, media)

sizeRules.title: Size Rules
sizeRules.help: Files outside this range will be ignored in the critical search

logDetection.title: Log Detection
logDetection.minSimilarHelp: Number of files with a log pattern to consider a directory a log directory

autoGitleaks.title: Auto GitLeaks
autoGitleaks.description: Automatically start a GitLeaks scan after the critical search
autoGitleaks.delayHelp: Wait time after the scan finishes before starting GitLeaks

info.title: How does Critical Search work?
info.description: The critical search scans directories looking for files that match the rules defined above. Unlike a normal scan, it ignores log directories and focuses only on potentially sensitive files. At the end, if enabled, it automatically starts a GitLeaks scan to detect exposed secrets.
